title: Deployment Snag Triage & Risk Sync — Private Deployments (VPC / On‑Prem)
content:
Meeting: Deployment Snag Triage + Risk Sync
Date: 2026-07-14 10:00-11:00 PT
Location: #private-deploys VC / standup notes doc
Facilitator: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya, Arjun, Sofia, Liam, Priya, Tobi (SRE consult), Elena (Solutions Eng — on call)
Absentees: none
Purpose: quick triage of current customer installation snags, align on mitigations, and capture high-risk items for escalation and playbook updates. This is a light-weight sync (30–45m) built to keep unblock cadence high during peak install wave.

Top-line summary (TL;DR):
- Four active customer install issues; two are network/VPC related, one is on-prem HA timing (k8s taint/scheduling), one is post-config regression in metrics exporter causing telemetry gaps.
- Immediate mitigations in place for customer A and C; customer B needs escalation to networking partner (customer’s security team) — ETA uncertain.
- Decision: for telemetry regression we’ll ship a hotfix branch + temporary metrics-sidecar fallback to avoid blindspots in the console.
- Action items assigned below; main risk is extended customer B install delay (could push revenue recognition by one month).

Notes (raw):
1) Customer: Alpha (large fintech, VPC) — BLOCKER (PD-842)
- Symptom: Persistent cross-account route issue between our peered VPC and customer production subnet; instances cannot reach kv-cache host on startup window, causing repeated node restarts and degraded SLO.
- Root cause hypothesis: customer route table missing propagated route, security team applied an egress policy that blocks ephemeral source ports used by our peer handshake.
- What we tried: validated SGs and NACLs from our side; tested handshake with ephemeral port logs (tcpdump) — packets hit customer edge then dropped.
- Next steps: Arjun to lead liaison with customer security; need their network engineer on a joint debug call (scheduled tomorrow 9am PT). Share traceroute + pcap.
- Temporary mitigation: move node startup to alternate bootstrap mode that retries with tunneled control channel (requires enabling feature flag in k8s manifest). Sofia to prepare simple toggle and fallback docs.
- Risk: if customer refuses config change, we will need to run Dedicated-hosted fallback (not ideal for compliance). Impact: SLA & billing negotiation.

2) Customer: Beta (on‑prem, regulated healthcare) — PENDING APPROVAL FROM CUSTOMER TEAM (PD-901)
- Symptom: Installer completes but control plane registration fails intermittently; error: "agent-register timeout 60s" on ~15% of nodes.
- Observations: failures correlate with environments that have internal proxy + strict MTU sizing. Install VM overlay uses 1400 MTU; customer infra uses 900.
- Hypothesis: fragmented packets causing our gRPC handshake timeouts.
- Work done: local test harnessed a 900 MTU VM and reproduced timeout. Patch created to lower chunk size for register handshake.
- Blocking: customer change board required to allow off-hours config tweak (proxy exception). Their change window is next Friday; could delay by 6 business days.
- Mitigation: Priya to send short RFC + impact summary to customer SOC/Change board and propose a scoped configuration exception for the install window. Also provide a non-invasive manual register script (requires operator SSH).
- Business risk: potential delay in go-live; Solutions Eng to prepare compensation play if timeline slips.

3) Customer: Gamma (edge cluster, hybrid VPC) — MINOR, resolved
- Symptom: telemetry lag where per-route latency metrics were missing for 2 hours after deploy.
- Root cause: our metrics exporter suffered a regression in v2.7.1 where series label changed; backend ingestion dropped those series for a specific tag.
- Resolution: Hotfix merged (PR #314), rolled to canary and then to prod for Gamma. Also applied metrics-sidecar fallback for 24h.
- Follow-up: add regression test for label schema in CI (Liam). Also add a short blurb in release notes to call out metrics schema change.

4) Customer: Delta (pilot install, small AI startup) — NO ACTION REQUIRED (info)
- Installer notes show longer startup due to non-default GPU drivers; customer opted to delay driver upgrade. We advised next steps in playbook and scheduled checkpoint next week.

Operational items:
- Playbook gaps discovered: network troubleshooting checklist lacks a recommended tcpdump command for peered VPC handshakes. Action: Maya to update runbook section and paste canonical tcpdump flags + sample trace.
- Telemetry coverage: identify 5 critical series to always keep for post-deploy health checks. Action: Liam to propose list by 7/16.
- Canary policy: add an automatic rollback trigger on missing critical series for >10m during canary (SRE). Tobi to prototype alert rule.

Decisions made during sync:
- Ship metrics hotfix as stable patch (no longer hold for next minor). Rationale: visibility is critical for customer trust; sidecar fallback reduces blast radius.
- For repeated network policy blocks at customer edge, escalate to Solutions Eng for negotiation and move to Dedicated-hosted fallback only after formal decline.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we add a customer-network diagnostic agent (lightweight, optional) that can be run one-off to collect packet captures and MTU info? Pros: speeds triage. Cons: adding binary increases support surface. Action: quick spike (Arjun + Priya) to propose minimum viable diagnostic script by 7/20.
- Playbook: who signs off on recommending Dedicated-hosted fallback (legal or sales)? We need a clear approval path. Action: Maya to loop in Sales Ops and Legal on approval flow.

Action items (owner — due):
- Arjun Patel — coordinate debug call with Alpha network engineer, provide pcap/traceroute, and propose control-channel fallback toggle (due: 2026-07-15)
- Sofia Garcia — prepare k8s manifest feature flag toggle + docs for control-channel fallback; add rollback steps (due: 2026-07-15)
- Priya Nair — draft RFC for Beta change board and provide manual register script with operator instructions (due: 2026-07-16)
- Liam O'Connor — add metrics label schema test in CI, propose 5 critical series for canary rules (due: 2026-07-16)
- Maya Chen — update private-deploy runbook network troubleshooting section with canonical tcpdump and peering checklist; capture escalation flow for Dedicated-hosted fallback (due: 2026-07-17)
- Tobi (SRE) — prototype alert rule that triggers rollback on missing critical series during canary (due: 2026-07-20)
- Elena (Solutions Eng) — prepare customer-facing impact and compensation template for delays >1 week (due: 2026-07-18)

Notes to self / informal follow-ups:
- Keep a tight envelope on symptom reproducibility steps — capture exact timestamps for Alpha failure window to correlate with customer network change logs.
- For Beta, the manual register script should be as low-friction as possible; prefer a one-line curl with explicit chunk-size header if we can avoid an SSH playbook.
- Logs: ask Observability to retain agent bootstrap traces for +30 days for PD installs during this wave (request sent via internal ticket).

Next sync: ad-hoc tomorrow for Alpha network call (Arjun lead). Weekly sync moved to Tuesday 7/21 10am PT to reflect shifting customer availability.

Appendix (quick commands / refs):
- tcpdump sample for peering handshake: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -n -s 0 'tcp and (port 50051 or portrange 32768-60999)' -w /tmp/peer-handshake.pcap
- traceroute hint: use tcptraceroute to the kv-cache host on port 50051 to see edge accept/drop behavior
- CI test stub: assert(series.labels.contains("route_id")) — prevents silent schema drift

End of notes.

(Informal) quick status: team morale ok — small firefights but good cross-team response. Keep escalation tight; avoid switching to Dedicated-hosted unless customer explicitly rejects network changes.
